record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the eighth international conference on fuzzy set theory and applications
record.original_question: For continuous Archimedean interval semigroups S = ([0, 1], *, <=) with 0 as annihilator and no neutral element, which non-nilpotent interval semigroups do not admit any multiplicative generator f: [0, 1] -> R satisfying x * y = f^(-1)(f(x) * f(y))?

evidence.quote: We say that a non-decreasing mapping f : I -> R is a multiplicative generator of S if x * y = f^(-1)(f(x) * f(y)) for all x, y in I.
Problem 5.4. Characterize the non nilpotent interval semigroups which do not admit any multiplicative generator.

artifact.status_search_result: No web evidence was found of a published characterization resolving this question. The problem was posed as an open problem at a fuzzy set theory conference, and standard references on continuous Archimedean t-norms (which assume a neutral element) do not cover the no-neutral-element interval semigroup setting addressed here. Status appears unresolved, but this could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Triangular norms (Position Paper III: Continuous t-norms)
status_evidence.snippet: Continuous Archimedean t-norms split into nilpotent and strict classes; both admit additive/multiplicative generators in the t-norm (neutral-element) setting.
status_evidence.claim: Standard generator results apply to t-norms with neutral element 1, not to the no-neutral-element interval semigroups in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Archimedean semi-group - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Archimedean semigroups without idempotents are notoriously harder to classify.
status_evidence.claim: General classification of Archimedean semigroups without idempotents is incomplete, consistent with the problem being open.
